findings.title: `_find_drawer` leaves edge cases unspecified
findings.detail: The design doesn't say what `_find_drawer` returns for a `:PROPERTIES:` with no `:END:` before the next headline or end of file. Today's code walks to EOF in that case and inserts at `len(lines)`. It also doesn't say whether a literal `:PROPERTIES:` line inside a `#+begin_example` or `#+begin_src` block counts. State the choice, for example 'unterminated drawer counts as absent' and 'no special handling of blocks, same as `_drawer_id`'. Add one test for the unterminated case so the implementer doesn't invent behaviour.

findings.title: Replace-existing-key in a misplaced drawer isn't an acceptance criterion
findings.detail: Criterion 1 covers adding a new key to a drawer that follows body text. `_inject_property` also replaces an existing key (for example `:UPDATED:` bumped by `stamp_updated`, which relies on this). The test plan says 'one drawer containing both the old and new keys', but no criterion or test explicitly covers overwriting an existing key in a misplaced drawer. Add that case, and `stamp_updated` on such an entry, to the criteria or test plan.

findings.title: Behaviour on entries that already have two drawers should be stated
findings.detail: Non-goals exclude merging entries that already have two drawers, and the design says 'first block'. The spec should say that on such an entry the first drawer is edited, and that this may differ from the drawer `_drawer_id` and orgparse read for `:ID:`. It could also add a test pinning that behaviour (no new third drawer, and the first drawer edited). That makes the non-goal checkable.

findings.title: Criterion 3 describes existing behaviour
findings.detail: 'An entry without a drawer still gets one right after the headline (and after planning lines)' is a regression guard rather than new behaviour. That is fine, but the test plan should say it is a regression test. 'Planning lines' also means SCHEDULED/DEADLINE/CLOSED as matched by `_PLANNING_RE`, so name the regex for consistency.

findings.title: Rollout is silent on the offset note in `_inject_property`'s docstring
findings.detail: The docstring says only creating a property shifts offsets and that stamping callers do it last. Inserting into a drawer that sits after body text shifts offsets too, as it does for a drawer right after the headline, so no behaviour changes. The implementer should keep the docstring accurate when it is rewritten.
